This bug wouldn't be nearly as interesting if it "just" resulted in a memory leak. Memory leaks aren't considered unsafe in Rust because they can't result in UB in the same way as e.g., OOB writes. In fact, there are APIs accessible in safe Rust which explicitly leak memory! [0]

This bug is effectively a use-after-free, which is definitely something that the Rust compiler should catch.

> Would be cool to see clippy pick up on this bug in older versions!

No need for that. A future version of the Rust compiler that incorporates a fix should reject the incorrect code, so all you'd need to do is compile older code with that new compiler.

[0]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/mem/fn.forget.html

- once the Rust compiler is fixed, then all safe Rust programs exploiting the bug must now be fixed, or the compiler will reject them.

But a human in the loop to decide what to cut is tricky to replacd for lots of reason.

I'm not talking about pumped hydro.  Batteries have largely rendered that obsolete.  And batteries are scaling like gangbusters.

Realize that even in a fully nuclear powered world, huge amounts of batteries are needed.  Replacing every ground vehicle in the US with a 70 kWh BEV would require enough batteries to store about 40 hours of the current average US grid power.  So the scaling is needed regardless of the post-fossil energy source.

A longer term storage mode is also needed to deal with seasonal storage and covering rare Dunkelflauten as batteries are not suitable for that.  Fortunately there are multiple ways that could be handled, so it's a question of which is best.
